column2: The hinge day: a reported 6:25 PM Miranda, a sheriff publicly describing learning of the suspect at 8:02 PM, and a 33-hour manhunt narrative that has to fit around both. Custody is also what ended the foreign-nexus review.

One page stating what most independent investigators had concluded by July 2026 about what killed Charlie Kirk and what did not. The official account is a single .30-06 round; this is where the reasons for rejecting it are gathered.

A witness says he sent the FBI close-up 4K 60fps footage of the moment Charlie Kirk was killed, then was called repeatedly and asked to delete it. He says he kept a copy. Deletion over preservation is a transparency question, not yet a court finding.

Lasers, high-power microwave, and the Active Denial System are fielded and acknowledged. Sorting the acknowledged from the alleged is the only honest way to weigh the directed-energy claims that keep attaching themselves to this case.

The one fight where the U.S. government was forced to examine whether people can be injured at a distance by an unacknowledged capability. Nothing connects it to UVU; it is here because the record shows how agencies concede injury while contesting cause.

Dirt removed, a transport SUV released, cameras and SD cards gone, a body camera that stopped on the roof, a foreign inquiry halted. Each is a reported allegation, and the page groups them by the kind of cover-up alleged.

Butler in 2024 produced documented drone concern; UVU produced citizen claims and flight OSINT. A reported working theory ties them to the same group and the same method — advanced means, local blame. It is an allegation, not a verified position.

One jacket fragment, four lead pieces, and a .30-caliber class call that critics say names a category rather than a rifle. The page tracks the federal testing and the transparency fights around it, including a reported integrity concern over Exhibit 6A.
Four proposed federal laws aimed at forcing the files out — FBI and DOJ disclosure, intelligence disclosure, a mandated investigation, and investigators the public can actually trust.

Robinson was reportedly Mirandized around 6:25 PM on September 11. The Discord confession posts carry a 7:57 PM stamp. Who held the credentials to that account in the ninety minutes between is the question the public record does not answer.

Pulsed microwaves really can create sound inside a skull with no speaker and no ear involved — lab-proven, and studied since 1961. The page keeps that proven core separate from the full voice-to-skull allegation, and states plainly that nothing places such a device at UVU.

A former CIA officer describes a London walk-in held under hypnosis for roughly three hours, arm involuntarily raised, giving up details he could not consciously recall. It is his recollection rather than a verified record — and it is the closest public description of the capability a patsy theory needs.

The working memo for this whole section: five priority questions, each routed to the page that answers it. Its real job is separating the documented programs from the Robinson-specific claims — the distinction most online argument collapses.

Five stacked layers — historical programs, beamed audio, digital grooming, human handlers, and a purely physical frame — assembled into one theoretical model. The last layer matters most: a patsy framework works with zero hypnosis if the wrong body is on the video, and what actually killed Charlie Kirk is still contested.

The argument that the modern analog of MKUltra is not LSD in a lab but a feed and a private server: funnel, reinforce, split, trigger, scale. The commercial version of that pipeline is observable at scale; the assassination application is not.

MKUltra is declassified public record, which is why the programmed-patsy question does not get dismissed out of hand. The page also carries the "Alice in Wonderland" thread — overwhelm a person with contradictions until the first coherent story offered becomes their truth.

The hub for every behavioral-control thread in this case, ordered so the documented programs come before the case-specific claims. No page here finds that Robinson was mind-controlled; the section exists so readers judge the theories against the real record.

A January 22, 1954 CIA memo asks whether a man could be drugged during one social encounter and induced to attempt an assassination at a later date. It names a foreign official as the target and an American official as the fallback. The document is real.

Two incompatible stories run on the same Discord logs: a partner's breakdown pulling a quiet gamer into violent rhetoric, or ideology networks cultivated to produce usable shooters. The page sets them side by side and names the discovery that would break the tie.

Control shows up three ways — behavioral, narrative, and physical — and only the first involves hypnosis at all. That is the point of the framework: the patsy reading survives intact even if nothing ever touched Robinson's mind, which is where the physical arguments come in.

The state's own September 17, 2025 ATF report could neither identify nor exclude the seized Mauser as the source of the autopsy jacket fragment. The rifling matched "numerous makes and models" — a class, not a weapon. The defense reportedly calls that exculpatory, and it is a large part of why independent work has moved toward a device at the podium.

If the Mauser chain fails on the lab report, the energy, or the geometry, what fired instead? This page holds the proposed answers — a 9mm CornerShot from the tent, a suppressed small-bore, or no bullet at all, as in the exploding-mic theory.

An ATF examiner testified that dust and debris were observed inside the seized barrel, and measured the jacket fragment at .286 to .301 inches — under the .308 a .30-06 fires. The counterarguments are here too: a deformed jacket measures small, and a fired barrel still collects dust.

A claim recorded in the master file says a bullet was lodged in the wooden stage, and that it was removed. If a second projectile existed and left before independent documentation, it belongs in a chain-of-custody log nobody has produced.

The argument here is behavioral, not ballistic: you do not spend hours engraving messages into cartridges and then hide them in a towel in the bushes. The rounds were the one category of item left behind while the backpack and pants went along.

The government's kill chain needs three links — Mauser, Losee rooftop, fatal wound. This memo routes each link to the page that tests it, and lists the disclosure targets that would settle the whole argument in an afternoon.

The rifle was reportedly dropped in a wooded strip with buildings on either side. The official account puts a car in a UVU lot at 8:29 AM and never says when it left — and no cell-tower record filling that gap has been released.

The state's weapon: a scoped Mauser Model 98 in .30-06, tied to a grandfather and a World War I story. Commentators note the recovered rifle is a commercial 98 rather than a K98, and that M98 Mausers were not factory-chambered in .30-06 in that era.

Robinson's prints were reportedly not the only set on the recovered rifle, and no video shows anyone firing it. The rooftop-footage filmmaker, an experienced firearms instructor, reportedly says the gun and the outfit do not match Tyler.

A citizen journalist circles a wooded lot on September 10 aerial imagery and says a white Kia Soul turned around at exactly that spot that morning. No plate, no VIN, no registration — the page carries the claim and the missing links together.

Everyone argues about whether a rifle fits down a trouser leg. A gun owner in a circulated clip makes the sharper point: even if it fits, the scope no longer holds zero, and you do not take a once-in-a-lifetime shot on a rifle you have not sighted in.

A .30-06 carries roughly 3,950 joules; a 9mm carries about 482. Commentators argue a cervical strike at that energy produces catastrophic channel damage and pronounced back-spatter, not the restrained injury pattern described publicly.

A 5 to 9 degree downward shot from the Losee roof should meet face or jaw first. The reported entry sits between larynx and trachea, left of the spine — a far more straight-on path. The geometry is the argument.

Weapon and ammunition analysis in one place — the Mauser narrative, the inconclusive ATF comparison, the energy gap, the trajectory problem, and the alternatives proposed when those fail. Start here before judging any single ballistics claim.

If a sophisticated operation killed Charlie Kirk, some of the people who drew the cameras were not the killer. This page compiles those distraction claims — every one an unproven allegation, none a finding of guilt.

Reported testimony that an officer's body-worn camera stopped recording while he was still on the Losee roof. Footage of the minutes after the shot is among the most consequential material in the case.

Who found the rifle, when, after which K-9 passes, and how the towel-wrapped bundle was photographed and sealed. These are ordinary evidence-handling questions, and on the public record they are unanswered.

The July 2026 filing quotes the Medical Examiner directly, and the injuries run far wider than a neck wound: hemopericardium, bilateral hemothorax, subarachnoid hemorrhaging. The page asks which mechanism predicts that pattern without extra assumptions.

The State's own probable-cause brief says the bullet travelled downward, and says the left side of the vertebrae was obliterated from C7 up to C2. Critics say those two sentences pull in opposite directions.

Professional four-channel audio roughly forty-six metres from the tent, uncompressed at 48kHz. Analysts read three separated low-frequency events from it and place the loudest one at the stage rather than on the roof.

The RØDE Wireless PRO clipped to Charlie Kirk's shirt, and the argument that it — not a rooftop rifle — was the kill mechanism. Video, broadcast audio, procurement records, and post-event debris all feed the same hub.

The prosecution's motive case as reported — ideological opposition, partner grievance, online radicalization — set beside the citizen reframing of the same facts as patsy, courier, or manipulated participant. The page holds both and adjudicates neither.

No clinical forensic profile has been released publicly, which has not slowed the writing of profiles. The page catalogues them by tier, because profiling claims shape how physical evidence is received long before a jury sees it.

If a service participated, the expectation is non-retail hardware — CornerShot mounts, shaped charges, ARCAS-class systems — rather than a grandfather's Mauser. No public weapons examination confirms any of it at the scene.

Roughly twelve lieutenant colonels reportedly at the Army's intelligence school on September 8, a VIP flight out on the 9th, and a killing on the 10th. No released visitor log or manifest confirms any of it.

The prosecution's physical case needs the autopsy fragment tied to the seized rifle, and the state's own lab could not do it. Rifling consistent with numerous makes and models is a class description, not an identification.

Light shorts in the morning, a half-full student pack, and a long scoped rifle that has to reach a roof somehow. The volume argument is the sharp one: the roof figure's pack looks fuller after the change, not emptier.

Washington County protocol reportedly seizes a phone at Miranda. Miranda is placed near 6:25 PM; the Discord traffic is stamped 7:57 PM, 260 miles from campus. The page documents the timing conflict without asserting forgery.
The hub for every argument that Tyler Robinson did not cause Charlie Kirk's death — ballistics, acoustics, identity gaps, and the standard physical tests that were reportedly never run.

On the clips people are actually watching, the prone figure shows no clear muzzle flash and no obvious recoil at the public shot time. The page carries the ordinary technical explanations alongside the decoy reading.
Clothing that does not match, movement that reads as trained, and a filmmaker who reportedly says the person on the roof is not the man charged. Who that figure is remains the whole rooftop case.

An officer reportedly testified he found a screwdriver 15 to 20 feet past the roof railing, protected by crime-scene tape. Helicopter footage circulated afterwards is said to show neither. Two records of the same few square feet.
Frame-by-frame measurement of the running figure — ten or eleven steps from the alleged screwdriver drop point to the corner. The pace is the argument: it reads as rehearsed rather than panicked.

No counter-snipers, no Secret Service layer, and nobody tasked with the rooftops overlooking the stage. Critics note that is precisely the capability the official rooftop narrative would have required.

An infrared laser reflected on a phone screen reportedly traces back to a grey van under the tent tunnel, whose rear hatch opens about four seconds before the shot and shuts immediately after. Person of interest only — no accusation is made.

By the time the paving contractor reached the courtyard on Sunday, September 14, roughly ten inches of soil was already gone — taken by an earlier, still-unidentified crew described only as men working for the state.

Claims that U.S. agencies limited, steered, or obstructed public understanding — sealed warrants, a field-office leadership change a month before, and one named on-record voice saying the foreign review was halted.
Two shot times circulate, 12:23 and 12:27, and the difference is not cosmetic — every camera frame, dispatch entry, and acoustic offset is anchored to whichever one is right.
The 6:25 PM Miranda against the 7:57 PM Discord stamp, laid out as a timeline rather than an argument. Read it beside the surrender narrative and decide which entries cannot both be true.

Recruit or silence: the compiled claims that Robinson was watched and cultivated rather than self-radicalized, including search-traffic patterns investigators say appeared months early. No public record confirms any agency approached him.

The stairwell figure and the camera-tracked Tyler wear different clothes and carry different packs — one roughly half full, the other nearly full. The official reading needs the pack to get fuller after an outfit change.

Everything the record says about the Mauser attributed to Robinson — recovery, DNA claims, the inconclusive ATF comparison, and the preliminary-hearing testimony about what was found inside the barrel.

Bates 003996-R2 is a discovery exhibit: video of Robinson being read his Miranda rights at approximately 6:25 PM on September 11, 2025. If the Discord confession has one document-backed problem, this stamped exhibit is it.

Two weeks before the assassination, a Utah public figure engaged with a post about radicalization through Discord groups. The timing is recorded here as a reported coincidence, not as a claim of foreknowledge by anyone.

The hub for the official suspect: identity mismatches, the surrender chain, the Discord artifacts, the travel timeline. Charged, not convicted — and organised so you can see which parts of the account are documents and which are inference.

The majority citizen finding, stated plainly: a small concealed charge at the microphone or pendant explains the shirt movement, the missing exit wound, and the debris in the SUV better than a distant rifle round. The skeptic counterargument is carried on the same page.

The public confession is described as photographs of a roommate's screen, released in stages months apart, rather than original logs or seized devices. Discord itself later told reporters the planning messages do not appear on its platform.

Wound morphology, trajectory, and energy tested against one .30-06 fired from about 120 metres. The page is careful with the headline shorthand: could not be matched is not the same as affirmatively excluded, and it keeps both readings live.

Joe Kent ran the National Counterterrorism Center and says the FBI shut his Charlie Kirk inquiry down before the foreign-nexus leads were exhausted. He left the post to say it on the record, which is what separates this from anonymous speculation.

In the earliest on-camera interviews outside UVU, one description recurs with unusual consistency: shot directly in the heart. The page records the accounts as given and leaves the mechanism question open.

A placeholder is a figure whose story role is fixed before identification is proven. The released timeline already needs one outfit change to link the neighbourhood cameras to campus, and the surrender clothing needs another.

The campus system is the backbone of the probable-cause affidavit — a first capture near 11:50 AM, a pause at the tunnel stairs, the Losee doors at 12:02. What it never captured is anything settling how Charlie Kirk was killed.

Circulated booking screenshots describe an arrest for crime-scene tampering; a public-records response reportedly says nobody was arrested. Those two records cannot both be right, and that unresolved conflict is the reason the page exists.

An infrared laser reflected on a phone screen and a casing reportedly dropping downward are the two observations behind the CornerShot claim — hinged Israeli hardware firing 9mm from crowd level rather than a rifle on a roof.

A former Turning Point representative alleges new hires were taken to Arizona bars in rented vans and asked where they stood on Mossad and Israeli forces. It is a whistleblower claim, unproven and disputed, and it is filed beside the wider foreign-intelligence threads./Timeline/2025
column3: Every 2025 entry in one column — the legislative and appointment groundwork, the summer pressure campaign and flight activity, the September 8–10 cluster, and the aftermath. Read it when a claim needs a date rather than an argument.

column2: The court year. Judge Graf's rulings, the March fight to seal the inconclusive ATF report, the April discovery stall, a June contempt finding, and five days of preliminary hearing in July.

His own chronology rather than the case's: the 2012 founding, the Groyper wars, the 2025 break with pro-Israel donors, then hour by hour through his final seventy-two hours. The last stretch is where the two timelines converge.

The routing map for every Timeline page — 2024 signals, the July–September pre-shot arc, the day-of clock, the custody chain, and the legal and forensic layers after. Start here if you do not yet know which timeline you need.

Six days carry most of the case: the September 8 pro-Israel exit post, the September 9 meeting and the alleged text, the 12:23 PM shot, the surrender, and the charging. Almost everything else on this site attaches somewhere inside them.

The master chronology for the charged man, from September 9 through booking and into the capital case. The custody, Miranda and confession-order conflicts are shown rather than reconciled, because the public record does not reconcile them.
Hour by hour across September 9 to 12 in Mountain time, built from court filings rather than commentary. It is the narrow, document-anchored version of the four days everyone argues about.
Four independent lines of reasoning place the Miranda warning at 6:25 PM on September 11 — not September 12. That single hour decides whether the 7:57 PM Discord stamp is even possible.

The instrument that established the arrest, filed September 16, 2025. It is also the first place the government commits itself in writing to a theory of how Charlie Kirk was killed, which is why every later dispute runs back through it.

The forensic chronology: a May 2025 autopsy-photo law, a July 2025 medical examiner change, the operating-room and pronouncement times, and a report almost nobody has read. Dates first, conclusions never.

The September 11–12 custody chain minute by minute — the family call, the sheriff's 8:02 PM account, a 6:25 PM Miranda timestamp, and a booking sheet reading 10:00 PM. Set side by side, some of those entries cannot all be true.

Device data as chronology: the ping gaps in the charged route, the claimed foreign phones at UVU, the NSA retention argument, and the extractions. Almost every entry here is a claim waiting on one record nobody has produced.
Two clocks in one page — the millisecond acoustic sequence at 12:23:30 captured on the Canon XA55, and the month-by-month emergence of the transmitter, shirt-pull and burnt-object claims.
When each takedown, account action and search anomaly happened, ordered by date. Information control has its own chronology, and it runs alongside the evidence one rather than inside it.

Every timestamped frame the released timeline attributes to the charged man across September 10–11 — doorbell captures, campus cameras, the stairwell stills. Cameras record movement, not names, which is where the identity dispute lives.

What she said and released, in the order she released it: the September 9 three-sources claim, the donor texts, the flight-log episodes, the SUV photographs. Ordering the releases shows which claim was built on which.

What the police radio actually carried on September 10 — the 12:26 first report, an all-black suspect description, the 911 calls, the detention. Dispatch audio is the least edited record of that afternoon.

Docket by docket: preservation orders, the October 2025 protective order, sealed transcripts, the January 2026 discovery list, and the fights over what the defense actually received. What the public ever sees is downstream of all of it.

How the first thirty-three hours of coverage were consumed — a shout and a detention, a second detention and release, and two false in-custody news cycles. Attention is a finite resource, and this is where it was spent.

Motive that needs no foreign service: lone-actor narrative incentives, a succession announced within hours, insurance and audit pressure, and gag orders shaping which theories could be argued at all. Attributed claims throughout, and not one of them a court finding.

Four motive lanes kept deliberately apart — donor and Israel-policy friction, the reported death warnings, geopolitical context, and institutional incentives. Each is routed to the page that carries it, and to the disclosure that would settle it.

The whole calendar year in one scroll: legislative and appointment groundwork, the summer pressure campaign, the September cluster, and the autumn court fights. Read it when you want the year rather than the day.
One line in the file says foreign leaders met on U.S. soil that day. No roster, no agenda and no host unit has ever been produced — and the same date carries SU-BTT's claimed first American landing.
A date with a claim attached and no document under it. The page keeps the claim anyway, then lays out what July 2025 actually documents on either side — including a UVU event form filed that morning.

Two investigations ran side by side from the same second. One had press credentials; the other had flight trackers and scanner audio. The scorecard at the bottom shows which citizen claims later turned up in sworn testimony.

Forty minutes from the shot to the reported 1:03:30 pronouncement, and almost every minute inside it is contested — a private SUV instead of an ambulance, a Level IV hospital instead of the nearer Level II.
One aircraft, one day. An Army-contracted HADES jet reportedly made two low, slow passes near UVU, and the tracking accounts disagree about both the clock and the altitude by hundreds of feet.
The whole claim rests on ADS-B screenshots. The same-day tracker post names a civil airfield at Omaha; the later compilations name an Army base. The page shows exactly where the label changed.

The date has a hard docket anchor: the Discovery Protective Order that set the secrecy regime over the case. The same fortnight also carried a Medal of Freedom and an explosives-plant blast in Tennessee.
A timeline of holes rather than events. Every interval with no record and every record refused, ordered by clock position — so you can see exactly where the official chronology goes quiet.
Everything in the air except the two famous tails: a Provo departure with a dark ADS-B leg, Fort Huachuca VIP flights, an Egyptian cluster, and the arrival stack that landed after the shot.
The chronological hub. 2024 signals, the 2025 pressure arc, the day itself, the custody chain and the court years — plus the shot-time dispute every other clock depends on.
Nine weeks of escalation, from the July speaker fallout to the last appearance on Ben Shapiro's show. Read as one arc it is the strongest motive material on the site, and none of it names a killer.
Every official podium moment in order, including the custody claim that had to be retracted ninety-eight minutes later. What the public believed on any given hour was set here.
Every vehicle in clock order — the Challenger that arrives and never leaves the affidavit, the grey van, the SUV that carried Charlie and was later disposed of, and the rental cars issued at Provo.
The alleged egress minute by minute: the climb, the prone position, the drop to the grass and the run north. The feasibility objections sit beside each step rather than at the end.

What happened to the courtyard after 12:23. Cameras and SD cards removed, roughly ten inches of soil hauled away, pavers laid on a Sunday — and a lead investigator who testified he was never consulted.
Sixty-six seconds, reconstructed second by second. Security moves at 00:18, a bystander is already filming at 00:27, and "He's dead" is spoken at 01:06 — thirty-nine minutes before the pronouncement.
Every claimed 2025 movement of one Egyptian-registered Falcon, in date order. It sat at Provo the week of the assassination and left the morning of it, which cuts both ways — and the page says so.
The ten minutes nobody watches: Kirk on stage under the canopy, the wireless mic placed under his shirt, the camera and monopod positions, and the affidavit's rooftop intervals running in parallel.
The 12:24 descent, a wooded-area gun drop no camera recorded, a missing car-departure time, and a receipt 209 miles south. The escape leg is where the charged route stops being continuous.
8:07 AM to 12:22 PM, frame by frame — the doorbell captures, a clothing change inside an unfilmed 105-minute window, the backpack dispute, and the stairwell stills the FBI later called enhanced.
The state-level chronology: appointments, podium appearances, charging decisions, and the reported "by Monday" crime-scene deadline attribution. Utah's own officials, on their own clock.
The university's own chronology — pre-event warnings buried in records releases, the rooftop decisions, which camera feeds exist, and the high-definition footage that has never been released.
Where the accounts collide: shot time, wound location, call chains, custody hours. Both versions are printed side by side rather than reconciled, because the public record does not reconcile them.
The year-level router. 2024's search-trend anomalies, 2025's pressure campaign and the assassination, and 2026's court year — each with its anchor events and a way in.
Two porch-camera frames on one residential street, 8:23 and 9:57 AM, carry the whole morning chain. If the neighbourhood clocks are wrong, everything built on top of them moves with them.

Every lens that may have recorded September 10, routed in one table — doorbells, campus CCTV, crowd phones, broadcast rigs, travel-stop recorders. It also names the cameras whose files are reportedly missing.

Dairy Queen at 6:38 PM, a Cedar City Maverik the next morning, and a sheriff's lobby whose surrender footage is reportedly unavailable. These are the cameras that test whether the evening fits one continuous person.
A man filming himself in the seconds after the shot announces the shooting and asks viewers to subscribe. Presence and self-promotion only — nothing here suggests he knew anything in advance.
Seconds after the shot a man in the crowd appears to chant "USA." He says he was not cheering, and the page keeps both the footage and his answer in view.

He reportedly asked the last audience question before the shot, which puts him in every timeline of the event. The page keeps that documented role apart from the crisis-actor claims no official source supports.
Scanner audio put an unidentified man on a bicycle through Provo carrying a .177 break-barrel air rifle. An air gun, not a firearm — and a parallel weapon scare while the real search ran.

The routing table for every distraction figure: who is court-documented, who is unidentified, and who appears for presence only. One admitted diversion proves distraction happens; a coordinated roster would need dispatch logs.

Side figures pull police, cameras and scanners toward false leads while the real exit happens elsewhere. Most people catalogued here were cleared, released, or never identified — the label means officers spent time on them, nothing more.

A photographer positioned near a south door, and a page that deliberately stops there. The suspicions attached to him online are unproven, concern a living person, and are not reproduced on this site.

The day ordered by who pulled responders and cameras: a first custody within minutes, a false "suspect in custody" alert nineteen minutes after the shot, a federal announcement reversed ninety minutes later.

The thinnest entry in the section, kept only for completeness — one uncorroborated image-analysis line about a clip-on badge being removed. A plainclothes officer or an event lanyard would look identical.
Forty-three minutes north of Provo, a man reportedly told officers there was an APB out on him for UVU. The claim that matters is procedural: local police were reportedly told not to interview him.
